Thermal resistance networks are \"simpli: Thermal resistance networks assume 1D heat flow and neglect multidimensional effects. Ignoring multidimensional heat flow causes complex interactions with materials to be ignored, like uneven heat generation and material properties. These omission can lead to underestimating peak temperatures, overheating, or failure. For example, a battery pack or electronic module could overheat because of the simplifications made for thermal networks.

How would you explain the \"concept of t: The concept of thermal resistance is like traffic on a highway. Thermal resistance is the resitriction of "lanes" that will slow a system down. For example, a series resistance network will be like consecutive construction zones along a highway, while a parallel resistance network will act as alternate routes that heat flow can take to avoid crowded areas and take the path of least resistance. Furthermore, adding additional "lanes" to a highway is similar to increasing the thermal conductivity whihc allow traffic (heat flow) to move faster due to the additional "lanes".
